spec.design: Blocked-copying counterpart of legacy_minimum_reserve_frontier.json: identical reserve grid, $5,700 probe, pipelines, budgets, first-check activation and windows; the reference is the blocked maximum frontier, and matching settings must reproduce it and the blocked March review, including per-trade account assignments. Paired minimum/maximum daily withdrawal frontier on exactly the same reserve grid, product-specific frozen pipelines, budgets, first-check activation policy and eight historical windows as the prior maximum frontier. Both mechanisms are rerun to collect passive dispersion metrics. Common reserves compare policies; nearest realized average-capital matches are descriptive, not a causal isolation of dispersion. No pipeline retuning. All results are historical and in sample.

reference_spec.design: Blocked-copying counterpart of legacy_reserve_frontier.json. The pipelines, reserve grid, cliff probes and windows are frozen exactly as in the non-blocking study (chosen there as the best shared-seat daily-maximum pipelines), so only the copying rule differs. Daily maximum withdrawals, persistent demand, shared seat reservation, first-check activation or pass forfeiture. Frozen product-specific pipelines from prior shared-seat daily-maximum results. Every window starts empty with fresh owner funding. Post-startup deaths means all deaths after 365 elapsed days, including young replacements. All overlapping historical windows remain in-sample; none is a holdout. Full-tape cents around 6780.10 diagnose the known March 2026 event, not a recommended precision of reserve selection.
